question: Re-fetch the exact Gobhila II.8 capture: verify the three discrete naming timings and Oldenberg's explicit note to section 14 without turning translator grammar or a school prescription into independently read Sanskrit or universal practice.
source_locator: Gobhila Gṛhya Sûtra II,8 (Kâṇḍikâ 8, Oldenberg SBE 30, pp. 56–59, exact Wayback capture 20231003011254 of sacred-texts.com sbe30020.htm): §8 (p. 57) the three discrete timings 'ten nights … a hundred nights … one year' for the Nâmadheyakarana (footnote 57:8 labels the rite 'The Nâmakarana' and points to Khâdira-Grihya II,3,6 seq.); §12 (p. 58) sacrifice to Pragâpati, to the birth Tithi, to the birth Nakshatra and to their presiding deity; §14 (p. 58) name rule 'beginning with a sonant, with a semivowel in it, with a long vowel or the Visarga at the end, (and formed with) a Krit (suffix)'; §15 no Taddhita suffix; §16 girls' name of odd syllables ending in -dâ; footnote 58:14 'Sâṅkhâyana-Grihya I, 24, 4; Âsvalâyana I, 15, 4; Pâraskara I, 17, 2. In the text read dîrghâbhinishtânântam instead of dîrghâbhinishthânântam.'
source_excerpt: When ten nights have elapsed after (the child's) birth, or a hundred nights, or one year, the Nâmadheyakarana (or giving a name to the child, is performed).
retrieval_method: Live FetchURL of the exact pinned Wayback snapshot URL (timestamp 20231003011254) on 2026-10-17; the full Kâṇḍikâ 8 chapter text with footnotes was returned, not a search snippet, and no URL wildcard or alternate snapshot was substituted. basis: The fixed question pins this exact capture, and the live fetch returned the full chapter with footnotes in which both tested items appear verbatim: the §8 clause naming the three discrete timings (ten nights, a hundred nights, one year) and the complete §14 footnote carrying both the parallel-school list (Sâṅkhâyana-Grihya I,24,4; Âsvalâyana I,15,4; Pâraskara I,17,2) and Oldenberg's explicit emendation instruction ('read dîrghâbhinishtânântam instead of dîrghâbhinishthânântam'). Support is scoped to this English-mediated snapshot of one school's prescription; translator grammar and the printed note are verified as mediation, not converted into independently read Sanskrit or a universal-practice claim.
limits: Translation-mediated throughout: Oldenberg's 1892 English via a Wayback capture of sacred-texts.com; the underlying Sanskrit was not inspected this pass, so 'sonant', 'semivowel', 'Krit' and '-dâ' remain the translator's grammar labels, and the §14 emendation is verified as a printed note (the translator's conjecture about the text), not as an independent Sanskrit reading. The footnote's Sâṅkhâyana/Āśvalāyana/Pāraskara references were recorded as reported bibliography, not fetched as inspected originals. This is one school's domestic naming prescription; its own footnotes record inter-school parallels and another school's divergent witness, so no universal ancient naming practice is established. 'Nâmadheyakarana' (sûtra text) versus 'Nâmakarana' (footnote label) is translator terminology, not a distinct rite asserted by this audit. The historical values attested here are exactly 10 nights, 100 nights, one year; any other number set used in fictional design work is an analogy and must not be attributed to Gobhila. Verdict is author-side evidence, not independent promotion verification.
